transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Sofia Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Nexa Head of ML), Priya Singh (Eng Manager), Michael Chen (Security)

Summary: Quick sign-off on POC success criteria and acceptance tests. Agreed on benchmarks (latency p95, throughput targets), reporting format (CSV + dashboard), and timeline for runs. Action items assigned to share runbook, traces, and security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right um good afternoon everyone thanks for joining. Quick roll call, I have Sofia from the SE team with me, can you say hi Sofia?
[00:06] Sofia: Hey all, hi, yep thanks Jordan.
[00:08] Alex: Alex here, thanks.
[00:09] Priya: Priya on the call.
[00:10] Michael: Michael here.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. So purpose today is to finalize the POC success criteria and acceptance tests we sketched earlier, and make sure we have a concrete benchmark plan and timeline. We'll go through workloads, metrics, pass/fail thresholds, and reporting.
[00:24] Priya: Sounds good, we want this to be clear because our execs will sign off based on those thresholds.
[00:29] Jordan: Totally. Starting with workload: Nexa said earlier you have two primary workloads: real-time clinical notes summarization at low latency and a batch inference rerank workload for search. Can you confirm the qps and sequence lengths?
[00:42] Alex: Yeah so realtime path is about 20 QPS averaged with peaks to 60 qps during morning, typical sequence length is 300 tokens, we do some longer ones up to 1k but mostly 200-400. Batch rerank is a backfill: 500 requests, each request runs 50 candidates so effectively 25k inference ops over a 2 hour window, done nightly.
[01:03] Sofia: Ok, good. For the realtime path we usually size for p95 latency not to exceed 200 ms for generation-only small responses, and for larger sequences we set a softer threshold, does 200 ms p95 align with your SLAs?
[01:16] Priya: Our internal SLA target is 250 ms p95 for on-path clinical features, but we'd love to get it to 200 if we can. Execs will sign off if we don't regress from current baseline by more than 5% and cost stays under expected.
[01:29] Jordan: Good, that's helpful. So let's define acceptance thresholds as a mix of absolute and relative: for realtime: p95 latency <= 250 ms (target 200 ms), no more than 5% regression in generation quality measured against your baseline eval set. Throughput: sustain 60 qps peak for 5 minutes without errors, and sustain 20 qps steady-state for 1 hour.
[01:49] Alex: Can we put a throughput target as sustained 200 QPS across a dedicated pool later? We're evaluating dedicated capacity but this POC is mostly on hosted and dedicated hybrid.
[01:58] Sofia: We can simulate both modes; for the POC we'll run hosted and a dedicated-like config (reservation/isolated pool) to show delta. We'll include both numbers in the report.
[02:08] Michael: On security, we need end-to-end encryption at rest, KMS integration, and full audit logs for the run. Also SOC2 compliance evidence for hosted.
[02:18] Jordan: Noted. We'll attach the security pack; Redwood Private supports customer KMS and on-prem if needed, and our hosted API has SOC2 attestation — I'll include the cert and the audit doc.
[02:28] Priya: Great. Back to acceptance tests: for batch rerank what are the go/no-go thresholds?
[02:33] Alex: The main concern is correctness and cost. We want the rerank accuracy (NDCG@10) to be within 1% of our current model and total nightly job to finish within a 3 hour window for performance reasons, cost ideally below $X per 100k candidates (we'll give you target numbers).
[02:49] Sofia: We'll run the rerank against your labeled test set, produce NDCG numbers, and measure wall-clock for the whole job under the same hardware profile. We'll also report tokens processed and cost estimate.
[02:58] Jordan: For acceptance let's set: batch job completes within 3 hours (hard), NDCG@10 not degraded more than 1% (soft but required), and end-to-end cost per run within the target you provide. If any hard threshold fails it's a go/no-go fail.
[03:14] Priya: Works for us. About quality/regression testing — how are you measuring quality? We have a baseline of automated evals plus human review for edge cases.
[03:23] Sofia: We'll run your baseline eval suite on both model variants we serve (original and quantized/optimized). We'll provide per-prompt deltas and aggregate stats. For human review we'll provide a sampled set of 50 prompts for you to check. If more than 5% of samples are flagged as unacceptable, that's a red flag.
[03:41] Alex: Important that the evaluation tool preserves prompt engineering context and any few-shot examples — that's where we often see regressions.
[03:47] Sofia: Yes we'll keep the prompt wrapper identical; runbook will show exact prompt/temperature/beam settings.
[03:53] Jordan: Ok next is benchmark plan and reporting: we'll do three phases — smoke (sanity), load (throughput/latency), regression/quality. Each run will produce a CSV with per-request latency, model variant, token counts, cost estimate, error rates. We'll also populate a dashboard (we'll share a link) and a summary PDF.
[04:12] Michael: Need the CSV schema up front so our compliance team can ingest — columns for timestamp, request_id, model_variant, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_code, region, run_id.
[04:24] Jordan: We'll include that exact schema; I will attach the spreadsheet.
[04:29] Priya: About timelines — what do you need from us to start?
[04:33] Jordan: Production trace (anonymized) and sample prompts, list of hot routes, and security questionnaire answered. If we get those by end of week (2025-07-18) we can schedule the first benchmark run the week of 2025-07-21 and have POC report by 2025-07-25. That gives a one week runway for runs and analysis.
[04:51] Alex: One week is tight but doable, we'll prioritize the trace. Also we want a final success criteria signoff doc by 2025-07-22.
[04:59] Jordan: That's fine. We'll draft the document and circulate it for signatures.
[05:03] Sofia: A few technical notes: we'll include KV cache tests for multi-step sessions, beam and temperature variations, and cold-start tests to see model loading times. If you use prefix caching in production we should include a prefix cache scenario.
[05:17] Priya: Yes we have a recommender cache and sometimes rehydrate keys, so that matters.
[05:21] Jordan: Regarding cost, do you want cost modeled per 1M tokens or per-night job?
[05:26] Alex: Both. Show per-token and per-run. For execs per-run is easier to understand.
[05:30] Sofia: We'll include both, and show delta between a baseline model and the optimized serving config (quantization, batching).
[05:37] Michael: A security question — will logs contain PHI? We need assurances logs are scrubbed and retained per our retention policy.
[05:44] Jordan: We'll run with PII/PHI scrubbed for the POC. For production, Redwood Private supports customer-managed logging and retention. We'll include that in the security appendix.
[05:55] Alex: On the go/no-go decision logic: who signs off? Is it just Nexa ML + Security + Redwood AE?
[06:01] Priya: Our sign-off will come from Alex and Michael, with input from engineering. Execs will give final approval if thresholds are met.
[06:08] Jordan: Great. So we'll define acceptance as: hard pass/fail items (batch job time, encryption and audit logs present, P95 latency hard cap for critical route), and soft items (cost, small quality regressions). If any hard items fail we mark POC as fail and propose remediation steps.
[06:25] Alex: Makes sense. Also can we capture the exact numbers in the doc: p95 latency 250 ms hard cap, 200 ms target; batch 3 hours hard; NDCG@10 within 1% degradation; quality regression not more than 5% on sampled human checks.
[06:38] Jordan: Yes we'll put those exact numbers in the signoff doc.
[06:42] Priya: For the reporting cadence — do you plan to share interim benchmark results or only final?
[06:47] Sofia: We'll share interim daily results during the load window and a consolidated report at the end. Also we'll push the CSVs to a shared S3 link (or your bucket if you prefer) and post the dashboard link.
[06:58] Michael: We prefer S3 in our account for security. We'll provide write creds for a pre-signed upload path.
[07:03] Jordan: Ok we can support S3 upload to your bucket. Add that to action items.
[07:07] Alex: One more technical ask: we'd like to test a quantized 4-bit variant — show accuracy and perf.
[07:12] Sofia: We'll include native FP16 and quantized 4-bit runs. We'll clearly label variants.
[07:17] Priya: That covers most things. Anything else?
[07:20] Jordan: I want to confirm acceptance reporting format: 1) CSV per-run with the schema, 2) Dashboard with filters by model_variant/run_id/region, 3) Summary PDF with pass/fail table listing hard thresholds and soft metrics. Agreed?
[07:34] Alex: Agreed.
[07:35] Michael: Agreed.
[07:36] Jordan: Great. Recap of next steps: Redwood sends benchmark spreadsheet, runbook, security pack by 2025-07-17. Nexa to send anonymized trace and credentials for S3 by 2025-07-18. We'll run benchmarks week of 2025-07-21 and aim to deliver final report by 2025-07-25. Final signoff doc by 2025-07-22.
[07:55] Priya: Ok we'll keep to that.
[07:57] Alex: Thanks everyone.
[07:58] Jordan: Thanks, I'll follow up with an email and attach the initial doc.
[08:02] Sofia: Bye all.
[08:04] Michael: Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional words are slightly off (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedicate), filler words present, speaker labels sometimes simplified.

End of transcript.
